answer:
# Inspection Authorization (IA) Qualifications Relative to Major Alterations — 14 CFR (eCFR)

**Answer in one sentence.** To *hold* an IA you must satisfy 14 CFR 65.91 (A&P mechanic certificate held at least 3 years, actively engaged in aircraft maintenance for the preceding 2 years, fixed base of operations, equipment/facilities/inspection data, and a passed written test); to *use* it on a major alteration, 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1) limits you to inspecting and approving for return to service an aircraft or related part/appliance **after** a major repair or major alteration that was done in accordance with Part 43 **and** with technical data approved by the Administrator, excluding aircraft maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program; and whether the work *is* a major alteration is classified under **Part 43, Appendix A**, with the general definition at **14 CFR 1.1**.

---

## 1. Scope and controlling framework

| Question element | Controlling rule |
|---|---|
| Who may hold an IA | 14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D — § 65.91 (issuance), § 65.92 (duration), § 65.93 (renewal) |
| What the IA may do with a major alteration | 14 CFR § 65.95(a)(1) |
| What counts as a major alteration | 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A (classification); 14 CFR § 1.1 (definition) |
| How the approval is executed/recorded | 14 CFR §§ 43.5, 43.7, 43.9, 43.13; Part 43, Appendix B (FAA Form 337) |

This is a statement of regulatory conditions, not an eligibility determination for any individual or a finding on any specific alteration.

---

## 2. Part A — Qualifications to *hold* an Inspection Authorization (§ 65.91)

An applicant for an inspection authorization must (PARAPHRASE — VERIFY against § 65.91):

1. Hold a mechanic certificate with **both airframe and powerplant ratings**;
2. Have held that mechanic certificate for **at least 3 years**;
3. Have been **actively engaged in maintaining aircraft for the 2-year period** before the date of application;
4. Have a **fixed base of operations**;
5. Have available the **equipment, facilities, and inspection data** necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or appliances; and
6. **Pass a written test** on the applicant's ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after **major repairs and major alterations** and for annual and progressive inspections under Part 43.

Note the coupling to the ask: the IA *test itself* is defined by reference to major repairs and major alterations. Major-alteration competence is a testable qualification element, not an add-on.

Application mechanics (not a qualification, but part of the process): application is made to the FAA on the airman application form (FAA Form 8610-1) and the test is administered through the FAA. **VERIFY** form number and current filing channel at the eCFR/FAADSS before quoting to an applicant.

---

## 3. Part B — The IA privilege that actually touches major alterations (§ 65.95(a)(1))

**VERIFIED QUOTE** — 14 CFR § 65.95(a):

> "(a) The holder of an inspection authorization may—
> (1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 [New] of this chapter, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator; and
> (2) Perform an annual, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection according to §§ 43.13 and 43.15 of this chapter."
> — eCFR, 14 CFR 65.95, https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.95

### Three cumulative conditions in § 65.95(a)(1)

1. **Eligible article.** The item is an aircraft, or a related part or appliance — **except** an aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness program under Part 121. The IA has no § 65.95(a)(1) approval authority over those Part 121 aircraft.
2. **The work was a major repair or major alteration performed in accordance with Part 43.**
3. **The work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator.** If the data is not FAA-approved, this paragraph does not authorize the IA to approve for return to service. Approved data must be identified (e.g., type certificate holder data, STC, FAA field approval, DER-approved data) — the specific approved-data vehicles are **PARAPHRASE — VERIFY** before use in a training or enforcement context.

### What the privilege is *not*

- It is an **approval-after-the-fact** authority: the IA inspects the completed major repair/alteration and approves for return to service. It is **not** a statement that the IA is the only person who may *perform* a major alteration, and it is not a qualification-to-perform rule.
- The IA's own authority to *perform* alteration work derives from the mechanic certificate (Part 65 mechanic privileges), not from the IA.
- Boundary point intentionally **not** asserted here: whether an A&P mechanic **without** an IA may approve a major alteration for return to service. That turns on the precise text of § 43.7 and current FAA guidance; **verify § 43.7 before relying on either answer.**

---

## 4. Part C — What "major alteration" means (the classification the IA must apply)

**Primary source for classification: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A.** Use Appendix A, not the short general definition in § 1.1, when classifying under the Part 43 / § 65.95 framework — § 65.95(a)(1) expressly points back to Part 43.

**VERIFIED QUOTE** — Part 43, Appendix A (airframe major alterations, opening text and first three items):

> "Alterations of the following parts and alterations of the following types, when not listed in the aircraft specifications issued by the FAA, are airframe major alterations:
> (i) Wings.
> (ii) Tail surfaces.
> (iii) Fuselage."
> — 14 CFR Part 43, App. A (GovInfo CFR-2024-title14-vol1, Part 43 App. A)

**PARAPHRASE — VERIFY**: Appendix A continues with additional airframe items (e.g., engine mounts; control systems; landing gear; hull or floats; airframe elements including spars, ribs, fittings, shock absorbers, bracing, cowling, fairings, balance weights; hydraulic and electrical actuating systems; rotor blades; changes to empty weight/balance increasing maximum certificated weight or CG limits; changes to basic design of fuel, oil, cooling, heating, cabin pressurization, electrical, hydraulic, de-icing, or exhaust systems; changes to wings or fixed/movable control surfaces affecting flutter and vibration), plus separate **powerplant major alterations**, **propeller major alterations**, and **appliance major alterations** categories. Do not quote these from memory — pull the current Appendix A text.

**General definition — 14 CFR § 1.1 (PARAPHRASE — VERIFY)**: a major alteration is an alteration not listed in the aircraft, aircraft engine, or propeller specifications that (1) might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness; or (2) is not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations.

**Practical rule for the IA:** classify under Appendix A first (enumerated parts/types → major). If not enumerated, test against § 1.1. The Appendix A / § 1.1 interaction is the single most common source of misclassification.

---

## 5. Part D — Documentation chain that accompanies the approval

The following are the expected companions to a § 65.95(a)(1) approval. They are **PARAPHRASE — VERIFY**; only § 65.95(a) and the Appendix A excerpt above are verified quotes in this document.

| Cite | Requirement (paraphrase) |
|---|---|
| § 43.3 | Persons authorized to maintain, rebuild, alter, or perform preventive maintenance; major alterations are listed in Appendix A |
| § 43.5 | No approval for return to service after maintenance/alteration unless the required record entries are made |
| § 43.7 | Persons authorized to approve for return to service after maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration |
| § 43.9 | Content, form, and disposition of maintenance record entries; signature and certificate number constitute the approval for return to service |
| § 43.13 | Work must be done using methods/techniques/practices in current manufacturer's manuals or other data acceptable to or approved by the Administrator, and to at least the original or properly altered condition |
| Part 43, App. B | Recording of major repairs and major alterations — FAA Form 337 executed by the person performing the work |

**Compliance checklist for an IA approving a major alteration for return to service:**
1. Confirm the item is not a Part 121 continuous-airworthiness aircraft. *(§ 65.95(a)(1))*
2. Confirm the alteration is "major" under Part 43 App. A / § 1.1. *(App. A; § 1.1)*
3. Confirm the alteration was performed using **technical data approved by the Administrator** — identify the data and its approval basis. *(§ 65.95(a)(1))*
4. Confirm workmanship and performance rules were met. *(§ 43.13)*
5. Confirm FAA Form 337 is executed where required. *(Part 43, App. B)*
6. Make the maintenance record entry with signature, certificate number, and certificate type. *(§ 43.9; § 43.5)*
7. Confirm weight-and-balance / flight-characteristic effects addressed, including test flight where applicable. *(§ 43.7 — verify exact paragraph)*

---

## 6. Part E — Currency and renewal, including the major-alteration activity credit

| Cite | Requirement (PARAPHRASE — VERIFY) |
|---|---|
| § 65.92 | Each inspection authorization **expires on March 31 of each odd-numbered year**, unless surrendered, suspended, revoked, or a different termination date is established |
| § 65.93(a) | Renewal for the next 2-year period requires activity at the rate of one qualifying event per 90 days the authorization was held — one of: (1) at least one **annual inspection** per 90 days; (2) at least **two major repairs or major alterations** per 90 days; or (3) at least two **progressive inspections** performed or supervised per 90 days |
| § 65.93 | Renewal also requires completion of at least **16 hours of training in the 24 months** before expiration, in specified subject areas (verify the enumerated areas and whether the requirement sits in § 65.93(a) or (b)) |

**Direct tie to the ask:** performing major repairs or major alterations is itself a **renewal-credit activity** under § 65.93(a)(2). So major alterations appear in the IA scheme twice — as the subject matter of the § 65.91(a)(6) test and the § 65.95(a)(1) privilege, and as the currency activity under § 65.93(a)(2).

---

## 7. Citation table

| Cite | Subject | eCFR URL | Status in this document |

| 14 CFR 65.91 | IA issuance/eligibility | https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.91 | PARAPHRASE — VERIFY |
| 14 CFR 65.92 | IA duration | https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.92 | PARAPHRASE — VERIFY |

| 14 CFR 65.95(a) | IA privileges (major repair/alteration RTS) | https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.95 | **VERIFIED QUOTE** |
| 14 CFR 43.3 | Persons authorized to alter | https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-43/section-43.3 | PARAPHRASE — VERIFY |

- **Verified by fetched text:** § 65.95(a) in full; the opening line and items (i)–(iii) of the Part 43 Appendix A airframe major-alteration list.

These are stated as paraphrases of stable, long-standing regulation and must be confirmed against the eCFR pages cited before being quoted in an exam answer, a training product, or a compliance record.

answer:
# Inspection Authorization (IA) and Major Alterations — 14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D

**Answer identifier: 14 CFR 65.91(c) + 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1)** (with 14 CFR 43.5, 43.7, 43.9, Part 43 Appendix A and B, 14 CFR 1.1, and 14 CFR 21.93 / Part 21 Subpart E as cross-references).

## 0. The answer in one paragraph

An inspection authorization is not a stand-alone certificate — it is an authorization added to a mechanic certificate holding both Airframe and Powerplant ratings. Two separate "qualifications" questions attach to major alterations and they must not be conflated:

1. **What qualifies a person to hold an IA at all** — 14 CFR 65.91(c), five elements, one of which (the written test, 65.91(c)(5)) is *specifically* about returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations. That is the direct regulatory link between the IA credential and major alterations.
2. **What must be satisfied for that IA holder to approve and return to service a specific major alteration** — 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1): the alteration must have been accomplished **in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**, and the aircraft must **not** be one maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program under 14 CFR 121.367 or 135.411(a)(2).

The IA never approves the alteration's *design data*. Design approval comes from an STC, a TC/amended TC, or an FAA field approval (ACO/ODA/DER). The IA inspects the accomplished work for conformity to that approved data and approves the article for **return to service**, on FAA Form 337.

## 1. Controlling provisions

| Provision | What it governs |
|---|---|
| 14 CFR 65.91 | Inspection authorization: application; eligibility; duration of the test process |
| 14 CFR 65.92 | Duration/expiration of the authorization |
| 14 CFR 65.93 | Renewal |
| 14 CFR 65.95 | Privileges and limitations (the major-alteration authority) |
| 14 CFR 43.5 | Approval for return to service |
| 14 CFR 43.7 | Persons authorized to approve for return to service (an A&P may **not** approve after a major repair or major alteration) |
| 14 CFR 43.9 | Content/form/disposition of maintenance records |
| 14 CFR Part 43, App. A | Major alteration classification (airframe / powerplant / propeller / appliance + the airworthiness-effect catch-all) |
| 14 CFR Part 43, App. B | Recording of major repairs and major alterations |
| 14 CFR 1.1 | Definitions (major alteration) |
| 14 CFR 21.93; Part 21 Subpart E | Major change in type design; STC |
| AC 43-210A; FAA Order 8300.16A | Field approval process; approved-data expectations |

## 2. Layer A — Eligibility to hold an IA (14 CFR 65.91)

- **65.91(a):** application is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator (in practice FAA Form 8610-1, Airman Certificate and/or Rating Application).
- **65.91(b):** an applicant who meets the requirements of the section is entitled to the authorization.
- **65.91(c):** the applicant must —
  1. **(c)(1)** Hold a **currently effective** mechanic certificate with **both** an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective. (No IA without both ratings.)
  2. **(c)(2)** Have been **actively engaged, for at least the 3-year period before the date of application,** in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with the chapter.
  3. **(c)(3)** Have a **fixed base of operations** at which the applicant may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week — it need not be the place where the authority is exercised.
  4. **(c)(4)** Have available the **equipment, facilities, and inspection data** necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance. *This is not a one-time gate: it is a continuing condition on exercising the authority.*
  5. **(c)(5)** **Pass a written test** on ability to inspect according to safety standards for **returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations** and for annual and progressive inspections performed under Part 43. This is the provision that makes major alterations an explicit subject of IA qualification.
- **Retesting:** an applicant who fails the (c)(5) test may not reapply before a waiting interval (commonly 30 days). *See verification table, item V-2.*

**Practical note on (c)(2):** the 3-year clock is about *active engagement in maintenance*, not merely holding the certificate; applicants should be prepared to document it (employer letters, 8610-1 blocks, work records).

## 3. Layer B — Conditions on exercising IA authority over a major alteration (14 CFR 65.95(a)(1))

The holder may inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part **after a major repair or major alteration**, subject to four cumulative conditions:

1. **Correct classification.** The work must actually be a *major* alteration under Part 43 Appendix A / 14 CFR 1.1. If it is minor, the IA authority is not the mechanism — an A&P may approve under 43.7.
2. **Accomplished per approved data.** "…if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator." Acceptable bases include an STC, a TC or amended TC, FAA field-approved data (Form 337, block 3, executed by the ACO/FSDO/ODA), or DER-approved data accepted by the FAA. **AC 43.13-2 is acceptable methods/techniques for *minor* alterations and cannot be the approved-data basis for a major alteration.**
3. **Not a CAMP aircraft.** The authority does not extend to aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program under 14 CFR 121.367 or 135.411(a)(2); those flow through the operator's program.
4. **Personally performed, with the wherewithal to do it.** The inspection and approval are non-delegable; the holder must have the equipment, facilities, and inspection data required by 65.91(c)(4), and must be current under 65.92 and hold a current mechanic certificate.

**Documentation that accompanies a compliant approval:** FAA Form 337 for the major alteration (Part 43; see App. B); a logbook entry with the return-to-service statement and signature/certificate number (43.5, 43.9); weight-and-balance revision where affected; equipment-list and operating-limitations/AFM revision where affected; record retention per 14 CFR 91.417 (and 43.9 disposition).

## 4. Layer C — Currency gates that switch the authority off

- **65.92:** each inspection authorization **expires on March 31 of each odd-numbered year**, so the effective term is **up to about 24 months** — shorter if issued mid-cycle. The holder may exercise the privileges only while holding a **currently effective mechanic certificate**.
- **65.93 (renewal):** the holder must still meet 65.91 and must show qualifying activity during the **24 months before the expiration date**. The recognized options are activity-based (historically expressed as one annual inspection per 90 days held, two major repairs/major alterations per 90 days held, or one progressive inspection) or training-based (**a minimum of 16 hours of training in the 24 months** — i.e., 8 hours per year — in accepted subject areas). Renewal is applied for on the prescribed form before expiration. *See verification table, item V-1.*
- **65.95 administrative conditions:** a change of fixed base of operations must be reported to the responsible Flight Standards office before exercising the authority from the new base. *See verification table, item V-3.*

## 5. What an IA cannot do (the boundary that answers most real-world confusion)

| Not an IA function | Correct route |
|---|---|
| Approving the alteration's design data | STC (21.115 et seq.), TC/amended TC, or FAA field approval via ACO/ODA/DER (Order 8300.16A) |
| Approving a **major change in type design** (21.93) | STC or amended TC only — an ACO or an ODA holder with STC/TC authorization |
| Approving return to service on a CAMP aircraft (121.367 / 135.411(a)(2)) | Operator's continuous airworthiness maintenance program |
| Delegating the inspection/approval to another person | Must be performed by the IA holder |
| Returning to service an alteration accomplished without approved data | Refuse; obtain approved data first |
| Acting as a design approval (DER) function | Separate DER/ODA authorization |
| Using AC 43.13-2 as the basis for a major alteration | Not approved data for a major alteration |

## 6. Operating checklist (the procedure an IA actually runs)

1. Classify the change: major or minor, using Part 43 Appendix A and the 14 CFR 1.1 airworthiness-effect criteria (weight and balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, other qualities affecting airworthiness).
2. If **minor** → not an IA matter; A&P approval under 43.7.
3. If **major** → identify the approved data *before* touching the aircraft. No approved data = no path to return to service yet.
4. If the change is a **major change in type design** → STC/TC amendment; stop the field-approval line of thinking.
5. Verify personal currency: IA not expired (31 March, odd years), mechanic certificate current, and the aircraft is not a CAMP aircraft.
6. Inspect for conformity to the approved data — structural, systems, finishes, clearances, torque, rigging — plus the alteration's effect on weight and balance, operating limitations, and equipment list.
7. Execute FAA Form 337: block 3 records the data approval (FAA/ODA/DER, where applicable); the return-to-service block carries the IA's signature and certificate number.
8. Make the 43.5/43.9 logbook entry with the approved return-to-service statement.
9. Revise weight and balance, equipment list, and AFM/operating limitations as required by the alteration.
10. Distribute and retain records (43.9; 91.417).

## 7. Verification items to run against eCFR before publishing or relying

| # | Check | Why |
|---|---|---|
| V-1 | 65.93(a) exact renewal options, paragraph letters, and the **16 hours / 24 months** figure | This is the part of Subpart D with recent amendment activity; the activity-based 90-day benchmarks may be numbered or phrased differently than stated here |
| V-2 | 65.91(d)/(e) retest waiting interval after a failed (c)(5) test (stated here as 30 days) | Confirm interval and whether a longer interval applies after a second failure |
| V-3 | 65.95 subsection letters for the fixed-base-of-operations notification | Privilege text in (a)(1) is stable; the administrative subsections should be cited by their current letters |
| V-4 | Part 43 pinpoint for the Form 337 requirement (43.5 and/or 43.9) | Cite the subsection actually carrying the 337 requirement rather than a general part reference |
| V-5 | eCFR revision date and any amendments with future effective dates | Confirm the text in force at time of use; use the eCFR point-in-time view if the alteration predates a rule change |

Cite as: 14 CFR 65.91, 65.92, 65.93, 65.95 (eCFR, Title 14, Chapter I, Subchapter C, Part 65, Subpart D), with the eCFR revision date stated in the work product.

## 8. Sources

- 14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-65/subpart-D
- 14 CFR Part 43 — https://ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-43
- 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A — https://ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-43/appendix-Appendix%20A%20to%20Part%2043
- AC 43-210A (Standardized Procedures for Requesting Approval of Data) — https://www.faa.gov/documentlibrary/media/advisory_circular/ac_43-210a.pdf
- FAA Order 8300.16A (Major Repair and Alteration Data Approval) — https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Order/Order_8300.16A.pdf
- FAA Field Approval process — https://www.faa.gov/aircraft/air_cert/design_approvals/field_approvals/field_approv_proc

## 9. If a narrower question was intended

- **Eligibility only** ("what do I need to get an IA?") → 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)–(5); identifier **65.91(c)**.
- **Privileges only** ("can I sign off this major alteration?") → 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1); identifier **65.95(a)(1)**.
- **A specific aircraft/alteration** → this is a compliance determination for that installation, which requires the actual approved data and aircraft records; it is outside what a citation summary can settle.

answer:
QUALIFICATIONS FOR INSPECTION AUTHORIZATION (IA) WITH RESPECT TO MAJOR ALTERATIONS
14 CFR Parts 43 and 65 — FAA AMT / mechanic-certificate context
Primary source: eCFR (https://www.ecfr.gov), current text as fetched 2026-11-15 per the source log; re-verify currency at the eCFR URLs in Section 9 before relying on this in a live compliance decision.

====================================================================
0. INTERPRETATION OF THE QUESTION (state this up front to the reader)
====================================================================
"Inspection auth" is read as the FAA Inspection Authorization issued under 14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D (§§65.91-65.95). "FAA-AMT" is read as the FAA aviation maintenance technician / mechanic-certificate context.

The question actually splits into two separate rules, and a complete answer needs both:

  (A) QUALIFICATIONS to HOLD an IA ......................... §65.91(c)(1)-(5)
  (B) The IA's AUTHORITY over a major alteration
      (what the qualification is FOR) ....................... §65.95(a)(1)

Plus a third, continuing layer: §65.92 (duration) and §65.93 (renewal), which is where major-alteration activity re-enters as a currency requirement.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
SHORT ANSWER (five lines)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with BOTH an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and in effect for a total of at least 3 years. [§65.91(c)(1)]
2. Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before applying, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under 14 CFR. [§65.91(c)(2)]
3. Have a fixed base of operations, reachable in person or by telephone during a normal working week, and have the equipment, facilities and inspection data needed to inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers and related parts/appliances. [§65.91(c)(3)-(4)]
4. Pass the IA written test on ability to inspect to the safety standards for returning aircraft to service after MAJOR REPAIRS AND MAJOR ALTERATIONS and for annual/progressive inspections under Part 43. [§65.91(c)(5)]
5. With the IA in hand, the holder may inspect and approve for return to service an aircraft or related part or appliance after a major repair or major alteration ONLY IF (i) it is not an aircraft maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program, (ii) the work was done in accordance with Part 43, and (iii) the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator. [§65.95(a)(1)]

Corollary that matters most in practice: if no Administrator-approved technical data exists for the alteration, the IA has nothing to approve against and cannot sign it off; the data must first be approved (STC, TCDS, AD, DER/ODA approval, or FAA field approval).

====================================================================
1. TWO QUESTIONS, TWO RULES — DO NOT CONFLATE THEM
====================================================================
| Question the person is really asking | Governing rule | What it governs |
|---|---|---|
| "What do I need to become an IA?" | 14 CFR §65.91(c)(1)-(5) | Personal eligibility for the certificate/authorization |
| "What may an IA sign off on a major alteration?" | 14 CFR §65.95(a)(1) | Scope of the privilege and its three conditions |
| "Who, other than an IA, may approve a major alteration for return to service?" | 14 CFR §§43.5, 43.7; Part 121 §121.379; Part 135 §135.437; Part 145 §145.201 | The general return-to-service authorization scheme |
| "How does an IA stay qualified?" | 14 CFR §§65.92, 65.93 | Duration and renewal |

====================================================================
2. PART A — QUALIFICATIONS TO HOLD AN IA: 14 CFR §65.91
====================================================================
§65.91(a)-(b) (procedure): an application is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator; an applicant who meets the requirements of the section is entitled to an inspection authorization.

§65.91(c) — eligibility. An applicant must:

(c)(1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with BOTH an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years.
   - Note the two distinct tests: both ratings must be CURRENT, and the ratings must have been IN EFFECT for a total of at least 3 years. Three years is the ratings-duration bound; it is not the engagement bound (that is (c)(2)).
   - An airframe-only or powerplant-only mechanic cannot qualify.

(c)(2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date of application, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with 14 CFR.
   - Two years is the engagement bound. It is measured backward from the application date.

(c)(3) Have a fixed base of operations at which the applicant may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week, but it need not be the place where the authority will be exercised.

(c)(4) Have available the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance.
   - This is the resource qualification, and it is the hook for the approved-data requirement discussed in Section 4: an IA who lacks the approved data for a given alteration is not equipped to approve it.

(c)(5) Pass a written test on ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations, and for annual and progressive inspections performed under Part 43.
   - The test is explicitly built around major repair / major alteration return-to-service standards. That is the direct link between "IA qualification" and "major alterations."

====================================================================
3. PART B — THE IA'S AUTHORITY OVER MAJOR ALTERATIONS: 14 CFR §65.95(a)(1)
====================================================================
VERBATIM (eCFR, §65.95(a), verified quote):

  "(a) The holder of an inspection authorization may—
    (1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 of this chapter, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator; and
    (2) Perform an annual, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection according to §§43.13 and 43.15 of this chapter."

[Editorial note: the eCFR rendering of (a)(1) shows a bracketed "[New]" marker after "part 43." That is an eCFR amendment/versioning artifact, not part of the regulatory text. Do not quote it as if it were.]

Decomposing (a)(1) — the three conditions are CONJUNCTIVE. All three must hold:

  Condition 1 — Aircraft category exclusion.
    The aircraft must not be maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under Part 121. If it is, the IA privilege in (a)(1) does not reach it; approval authority for that aircraft lives in the air carrier's program (see §121.379 and the operator's manual/procedures). Note the qualifier: it is "maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121," not simply "a Part 121 aircraft" in the abstract. Do not extend this exclusion to Part 135 — Part 135 has its own approval-authority rule (§135.437).

  Condition 2 — Performed in accordance with Part 43.
    The maintenance/alteration work itself must have been done under Part 43.

  Condition 3 — Done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator.
    This is the operative limit for major alterations. The IA is approving conformance to approved data; the IA is not the data approver. If the alteration was accomplished on the basis of unapproved data (e.g., acceptable methods under AC 43.13-2B alone, a manufacturer's service bulletin that is not FAA-approved, or a field-developed procedure with no FAA approval), the IA cannot approve it for return to service under (a)(1).

Also from §65.95(a)(2), separately: the annual-inspection and progressive-inspection privileges. These are distinct from the major-alteration approval privilege and are frequently confused with it.

====================================================================
4. WHAT "TECHNICAL DATA APPROVED BY THE ADMINISTRATOR" MEANS, AND THE DECISION PATH
====================================================================
FAA guidance (AC 43-210A, Change 1), verbatim:
  "...persons authorized to approve an aircraft or aircraft component for return to service after maintenance, preventative maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration. For major repairs or major alterations the work must be done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator."

AC 43-210 further identifies the rule basis for the approved-data requirement on type-certificated products as:
  - Part 43, §43.7(d) and §43.17(e)(2)
  - Part 65, §65.95(a)(1)

Approved data sources for a major alteration typically include: an STC (and its drawings/instructions for continued airworthiness), the type certificate data sheet where the alteration is covered, an AD, a PMA part installed per its approved installation data, a DER/ODA-approved repair or alteration drawing, or an FAA field approval (Form 337 block 3). AC 43.13-2 is acceptable methods/techniques/practices — for a major alteration it is not, by itself, approved technical data.

IA decision path for a major alteration (apply in order):
  1. Is the article a major alteration? Determine under Part 43 Appendix A (see Section 8).
  2. Does FAA-approved technical data exist that covers this alteration on this make/model? If NO -> stop. The IA cannot approve. Route to approved-data acquisition (STC/DER/ODA) or FAA field approval.
  3. Was the work actually accomplished in accordance with that approved data (no deviations)? If NO -> stop; the alteration must be brought into conformance or the data revised and approved.
  4. Is the aircraft excluded by §65.95(a)(1) (Part 121 continuous airworthiness program)? If YES -> stop; use the operator's approval process.
  5. Is the alteration within the IA's own capability and does the IA have the data, facilities and equipment (§65.91(c)(4))? If NO -> stop.
  6. Personally inspect; make the §43.9 maintenance record entry; execute FAA Form 337 as prescribed; ensure any operating-limitation or AFM flight-data changes are revised and set forth per §91.9 (the §43.7(a) preconditions).

====================================================================
5. PART C — WHO MAY APPROVE FOR RETURN TO SERVICE: §§43.5 AND 43.7
====================================================================
§43.5 (Approval for return to service after maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration): no person may return an aircraft, airframe, engine, propeller, appliance or component part to service after that work unless it has been approved for return to service by a person authorized under §43.7.

§43.7 (Persons authorized to approve ... for return to service):
  - Paragraph (a) sets preconditions for ANY approval: the §43.9/§43.11 maintenance record entry must be made; the Administrator's repair/alteration form (FAA Form 337) must be executed as prescribed; and if the repair or alteration changes operating limitations or AFM flight data, those must be revised and set forth per §91.9.
  - The remaining paragraphs enumerate the categories of persons who may approve — including the holder of a mechanic certificate for work other than a major repair or major alteration, the holder of an inspection authorization for a major repair or major alteration done per Administrator-approved technical data, and the certificate holders operating under Parts 121, 135 and 145 (and certain other authorized persons).
  - §43.7(d) is the paragraph AC 43-210A cites as imposing the Administrator-approved-technical-data requirement for major repairs/alterations.

CONFIDENCE MARKER: the existence and content of §43.7 and its role are certain; the individual paragraph LETTERS beyond (a) and (d) should be confirmed against the current eCFR text before being quoted in a filing. Section 9 gives the URL.

Key takeaway for the AMT audience: an A&P mechanic certificate, standing alone, is NOT authority to approve a major repair or major alteration for return to service in the Part 91 world. That authority sits with the IA (per §65.95(a)(1)) or with one of the other §43.7-listed persons. Performing the work and approving the work are different acts under different rules.

====================================================================
6. PART D — CONTINUING QUALIFICATION: DURATION AND RENEWAL (§§65.92, 65.93)
====================================================================
§65.92 (Duration): each inspection authorization expires on 31 March of each odd-numbered year — i.e., a 2-year cycle ending on 31 March of an odd year. (Confirm any additional reinstatement paragraphs on eCFR; the core expiration rule is as stated.)

§65.93(a) (Renewal): to renew for a 2-year period, the applicant must present evidence by 31 March of the renewal year that, during the 12-month period before the expiration date, the applicant has done ONE of the following:
  (1) Performed at least one annual inspection for each 90 days the applicant held the current authority; or
  (2) Performed at least two MAJOR REPAIRS OR MAJOR ALTERATIONS for each 90 days the applicant held the current authority; or
  (3) Performed, or supervised and approved, at least one progressive inspection in accordance with standards prescribed by the Administrator; or
  (4) Attended and successfully completed a refresher course acceptable to the Administrator of not less than 8 hours of instruction; or
  (5) Passed an oral test by an FAA inspector to determine that the applicant's knowledge of applicable regulations and standards is current.

Note the design of option (2): major-alteration activity is itself a qualifying currency path. "Two major repairs or major alterations for each 90 days" is an activity count for RENEWAL ELIGIBILITY — it is not an approval privilege and does not change the §65.95(a)(1) conditions.

====================================================================
7. PART E — RECORDS AND FORMS THAT ACCOMPANY THE APPROVAL
====================================================================
  - §43.9: maintenance record entries (description of work, date, name, certificate number/type where required, and for major repairs/alterations the reference to the approved data used).
  - FAA Form 337 (Major Repair and Alteration): executed by the person performing the work and, where applicable, by the approving person; per §43.7(a)(2) it must be executed in the manner prescribed by the Administrator.
  - §91.9 / §43.7(a)(3): if the alteration changes operating limitations or approved AFM flight data, those must be revised and set forth.
  - §91.417: Part 91 operator recordkeeping and retention for maintenance records, including Form 337 copies where applicable.
  - Parts 121/135/145 operators and repair stations have their own record and approval rules; do not import Part 91 practice into those contexts without checking the operator's approved program.

====================================================================
8. PART F — MAJOR vs. MINOR: 14 CFR PART 43, APPENDIX A
====================================================================
The major/minor line is drawn in Appendix A to Part 43 (Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance). Appendix A(a) covers airframes, (b) powerplants, (c) propellers, (d) appliances, and (e) defines major alterations as those that might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness, or that are not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations. The §65.95(a)(1) privilege is triggered only once the change is classified as a MAJOR alteration; a minor alteration is handled under the ordinary §43.7 mechanic-certificate path.

====================================================================
9. PART G — OPERATING-CONTEXT MATRIX (approval authority for a major alteration)
====================================================================
| Context | Who approves the major alteration for return to service | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Part 91 (general aviation) | IA holder, if done per Administrator-approved technical data; otherwise approved data must first be obtained (STC/DER/ODA/FAA field approval) | §65.95(a)(1); §43.5; §43.7 |
| Part 121 (continuous airworthiness program) | The air carrier under its approved program — the IA privilege in §65.95(a)(1) is expressly excluded for these aircraft | §65.95(a)(1) (exclusion); §121.379; §43.17(e)(2) |
| Part 135 | The certificate holder under its approved maintenance program / authority to approve | §135.437 |
| Part 145 repair station | The repair station under its certificate and privileges, within its ratings and approved data | §145.201 |

CONFIDENCE MARKER: the Part 91 row is verified from the eCFR quote and AC 43-210A. The Part 121 exclusion is verified from the eCFR quote. answer:
# Inspection Authorization and Major Alterations — Qualifications and Scope (FAA-AMT, 14 CFR)

Source of record: eCFR, Title 14, Part 65, Subpart D (Inspection Authorizations), read with Part 43 and Part 1. eCFR text as retrieved 2026-11-15; confirm currency at time of use (eCFR is continuously revised).

## 1. Short answer — the request contains two questions

**Question A — What qualifies a person to hold an Inspection Authorization (IA)?**
The eligibility requirements in **14 CFR part 65, subpart D** (shown on the current eCFR subpart-D page at **§ 65.71, 'Eligibility requirements: General'**). It is a mechanic-certificate-plus-experience qualification, not a separate license.

**Question B — What may an IA holder do with a major alteration?**
The authority is stated separately in **14 CFR § 65.95(a)(1)**: the IA may *inspect and approve for return to service* an aircraft or related part/appliance after a **major repair or major alteration**, done in accordance with **part 43** and with **technical data approved by the Administrator** — except aircraft maintained under a **part 121** continuous-airworthiness program.

An IA is therefore **an approval/return-to-service authority**, not a qualification to *perform* the alteration. The alteration itself is performed by persons authorized under part 43 (§ 43.3) using approved data.

## 2. Eligibility qualifications (Question A)

| # | Qualification | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hold a mechanic certificate with **both Airframe and Powerplant ratings** | 14 CFR part 65 subpart D |
| 2 | Have **held** that mechanic certificate for at least **3 years** | 14 CFR part 65 subpart D |
| 3 | Have been **actively engaged in maintaining aircraft** for at least **2 of the last 3 years** before applying | 14 CFR part 65 subpart D |
| 4 | Have a **fixed base of operations** — facilities, equipment, and records sufficient to perform inspections, from which the IA is available | 14 CFR part 65.95 / subpart D |
| 5 | Apply to the responsible **FSDO** on **FAA Form 8610-2**; the FSDO reviews eligibility and issues or denies the authorization (an interview may be required) | 14 CFR part 65 subpart D; FAA IA Information Guide |
| 6 | **Renewal** (continued qualification): biennial, falling in **odd-numbered years** with a **March 31** deadline, satisfied by recent inspection experience or by completing **8 hours** of refresher/update training | 14 CFR part 65 subpart D |

**What is *not* an eligibility requirement:** there is no requirement that the applicant be employed by a repair station, hold a type rating, or hold an A&P plus an avionics/other rating. The A&P + 3-year + 2-of-3 active-engagement test is the gate.

**Documentation to take to the FSDO:** current mechanic certificate (A&P), evidence of the 3-year holding period, evidence of active engagement in 2 of the last 3 years (employer/repair-station letters, work records), and a description of the fixed base of operations with its equipment and records.

## 3. Major-alteration authority and its conditions (Question B)

Governing text — **14 CFR § 65.95(a)(1)**:

> '(a) The holder of an inspection authorization may— (1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator...'

Four conditions must all be satisfied before an IA signs off a major alteration:

1. **The item is a 'major alteration'** as defined — an alteration in powerplant, airframe, propeller, or appliance that might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness (14 CFR § 1.1), with the illustrative list in **part 43, Appendix A**.
2. **Approved technical data** — the work must have been done in accordance with data **approved by the Administrator** (STC, amended TC, or other FAA-approved data). The IA cannot create or self-approve design data; where no approved data exists, the installer must obtain it (STC/field approval) before the IA can approve for return to service. See AC 43-210A for acceptable methods, techniques, and practices.
3. **Part 43 compliance** — the alteration conforms to the applicable part 43 performance rules and the work was performed by persons authorized under part 43.
4. **Not a part 121 continuous-airworthiness aircraft** — excluded from IA approval by the parenthetical in § 65.95(a)(1); such aircraft are handled under the operator's continuous-airworthiness program/repair station.

**Recording:** a major alteration requires completion of **FAA Form 337** (Major Repair and Alteration) under **part 43, Appendix B**, submitted to the FSDO — the appendix sets a **48-hour** window after approval for return to service. A return-to-service entry is made in the maintenance record.

**Major repair vs. major alteration:** both are covered by the same § 65.95(a)(1) authority and the same approved-data test; the distinction matters for the definitional trigger (Appendix A) and for Form 337 block entries, not for the IA's basic authority.

## 4. Common compliance failures (audit-facing)

- Treating the IA as authority to **perform** the alteration rather than to **inspect and approve for return to service** it.
- Approving an alteration supported only by owner-produced or unapproved data (no STC/approved data).
- Approving a major alteration on an aircraft maintained under a **part 121** continuous-airworthiness program.
- Missing or incorrectly completed **Form 337** / no return-to-service entry.
- Approving outside the IA's rating scope (airframe vs. powerplant vs. propeller/appliance).
- Lapsed IA (missed the odd-year March 31 renewal).

## 5. Verify at time of use

Pull `https://ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-65/subpart-D` and `https://ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-43` and record the eCFR 'current as of' date. Confirm the section numbers for the eligibility criteria (§ 65.71 as shown on the retrieved subpart-D page) against the live text, because part 65 has been reorganized historically and section numbers have shifted. Cross-check with the local FSDO and the current FAA IA Information Guide.
